body:
Hmmm, testing this on master the default action map seems to be correct.

`/user/eyes_ext` is correctly included in the `default_pose` definition, and bound to `/interaction_profiles/ext/eye_gaze_interaction`.

There is no entry for the HTC tracker so either you are misinterpreting the action map, we already fixed this issue, or the action map is correct but the Vive implementation is having a hissy fit.

Ah!  I definitely misplaced my confidence there, I am *so* sorry (I irresponsibly assumed during my code search that the proximity of all the `vive_tracker_htcx` roles was significant due to the behaviour I was seeing, and eagerly submitted a report and proposed solution that worked after only narrow testing - without reading the suspected context 🤦‍♀️)

Here is what I can confidently (responsibly) say:  I experience the issue with the default action map, and the issue resolves upon removal of all the other `default_pose` actions, or from disabling eye tracking in some way *(such as removing the `default_pose` from the "Eye gaze" profile, disabling the "Eye Gaze Interaction" extension in Godot, or disabling the OpenXR API layer via SteamVR's UI)*

To be more detailed, there are actually two types of conflicts that enabling eye tracking introduces in my setup:

1. Enabling eye tracking produces the following outputs (which are for all of the default profiles except for eye gaze):  
`OpenXR: failed to suggest bindings for  /interaction_profiles/khr/simple_controller ! [ XR_ERROR_HANDLE_INVALID ]`  
`OpenXR: failed to suggest bindings for  /interaction_profiles/htc/vive_controller ! [ XR_ERROR_HANDLE_INVALID ]`  
`OpenXR: failed to suggest bindings for  /interaction_profiles/microsoft/motion_controller ! [ XR_ERROR_HANDLE_INVALID ]`  
`OpenXR: failed to suggest bindings for  /interaction_profiles/oculus/touch_controller ! [ XR_ERROR_HANDLE_INVALID ]`  
`OpenXR: failed to suggest bindings for  /interaction_profiles/valve/index_controller ! [ XR_ERROR_HANDLE_INVALID ]`  
`OpenXR: failed to suggest bindings for  /interaction_profiles/hp/mixed_reality_controller ! [ XR_ERROR_HANDLE_INVALID ]`  
`OpenXR: failed to suggest bindings for  /interaction_profiles/htc/vive_cosmos_controller ! [ XR_ERROR_HANDLE_INVALID ]`  
`OpenXR: failed to suggest bindings for  /interaction_profiles/htc/vive_focus3_controller ! [ XR_ERROR_HANDLE_INVALID ]`  
`OpenXR: failed to suggest bindings for  /interaction_profiles/htc/vive_tracker_htcx ! [ XR_ERROR_HANDLE_INVALID ]`  
*(disabling eye tracking, or removing `default_pose` from the above profiles silences the error)*
3. The HTC Vive Tracker using `default_pose` generates a firehose of:  
`OpenXR: couldn't create action space! [ XR_ERROR_HANDLE_INVALID ]`  
when eye tracking is fully enabled.

So, all that to say: I am experiencing a conflict between `default_pose` being used in any profile at the same time it is used in the "Eye gaze" profile, specifically when the `XR_EXT_eye_gaze_interaction` OpenXR extension is enabled *(possibly specific to the Vive Console for SteamVR implementation of the eye gaze extension)*.

Apologies again for the noise of my initial submission - I will be certain to be more objective without assumptions in future reports.

Quick update: It seems that adding a pose action called `eye_pose` to the action map, and replacing `default_pose` with `eye_pose` for the "Eye gaze" profile resolves the issue, and eye tracking still works...!

I tried this per [a suggestion you made on the Godot forums last year](https://forum.godotengine.org/t/eye-tracker-support-for-htc-vive-pro-eye/56755/2).

This even appears to be the suggestion [in the Godot documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/xr/openxr_settings.html#eye-gaze-interaction) as well.

So, in an ironic twist for the erroneously proposed solution, perhaps the issue *does* lie within the "Eye gaze" profile using `default_pose`?  Where, at least in my setup, it instead requires a separate pose to be defined for itself.

Note that the issue of the default action map causing problems with eye tracking in my situation still stands.

Hmmm, I'm guessing because we add `/user/eyes_ext` to the potential list of paths for the `default_pose` is what is causing the issues. It shouldn't, it doesn't break the OpenXR spec, but I guess some runtimes get confused by it.

In hindsight the default pose has been more trouble than its worth.

I guess we could make an `eye_pose` action instead that is only used for the eye tracking. It just means people need to know they must select this pose (I really need to find the time to improve the action system in this respect).
